answer: Require each agent to lock a bonded deposit before it can vote, and make voting weight grow only as the square root of that stake. An attacker who floods the network with an ocean of cheap identities finds every one demands fresh collateral, yet their pooled influence barely rises above a flat mesa. The honest tide of long-bonded agents keeps majority weight, so minting thousands of sybils costs quadratically more capital than the sliver of power it actually buys.
